steps.hook: POV: you said "yeah, I'm good" while your chest was caving in.

steps.alt_text: Man in a crowd looking down alone dark cinematic. Overlay text reads: ...

steps.caption:
Saying you're fine when you're falling apart doesn't make you fake. It makes you exhausted. Your brain learned that showing panic gets you judged, so it forces you to perform calm while your chest tightens and your pulse hammers in your ears.
If you smile through the whole day at work and shut down the second you get home alone, you're not alone. That's what high-functioning social anxiety actually looks like.
Comment MASK and I'll send you the full breakdown - why your body stays in survival mode even when you're safe, and why performing "fine" costs you everything after.

steps.hook: POV: the conversation pauses and your throat locks shut.

steps.alt_text: Man frozen mid conversation with someone dark cinematic. Overlay text ...

steps.caption:
That blank isn't you being slow or stupid. It's your nervous system pulling the emergency brake the second silence hits, because silence feels like a spotlight about to expose you. Your throat tightens, your heart spikes, and the words you had get locked behind a body that thinks it's safer to say nothing.
If you sit there nodding while the sentence dies in your chest and then say the perfect version out loud in the car later, you're not alone. This is what social anxiety really looks like at 1am.
The words don't disappear. They just come back when there's no one left to hear them. Comment BLANK and I'll send you the full breakdown - why the freeze happens and why the replay never stops.
#socialanxiety #overthinking #socialanxietystruggles #anxietyproblems #introvertstruggles #latenightthoughts
